evals.name: build-graph-from-corpus
evals.prompt: we've got a couple years of incident postmortems sitting in a folder and our RAG setup keeps whiffing on the questions we actually care about — stuff like 'which teams keep getting burned by the same dependency'. it retrieves the right-ish documents but never connects them. i put 5 sample postmortems in CORPUS_PATH. can you build me something that turns these into a graph i can actually traverse? the entity types that matter to us are services, incidents, teams and components, not the generic person/org/location stuff.
evals.expected_output: A working extraction pipeline using domain entity types (SERVICE/INCIDENT/TEAM/COMPONENT), producing a graph where surface-form variants are resolved to single nodes.
assertions: Uses the user's domain entity types (SERVICE/INCIDENT/TEAM/COMPONENT) rather than the generic PERSON/ORGANIZATION/LOCATION set
Includes an explicit entity-resolution stage that merges surface-form variants into canonical nodes
Constrains extraction with a schema (Pydantic model or JSON schema) instead of parsing free text or regex
Preserves edge direction and allows multiple distinct predicates between the same pair (MultiDiGraph or equivalent)
Tags entities and relations with their source document so facts are traceable
Instructs the extractor to emit a per-entity description usable for disambiguation
Delivered code is syntactically valid Python

evals.name: diagnose-fragmented-graph
evals.prompt: i built a knowledge graph out of our postmortems and multi-hop queries keep coming back empty or useless. example: 'which teams are connected to incidents involving the redis cluster' returns basically nothing, even though i can eyeball the graph and see all the pieces are in there somewhere. the graph is at GRAPH_PATH. what's actually wrong with it and how do i fix it?
evals.expected_output: Identifies unresolved duplicate entities (J. Okonkwo/Jane Okonkwo, ledger-api/Ledger API, Meridian Payments/MP checkout, R./Rosa Vasquez) splitting the graph into 4 disconnected components, and prescribes entity resolution.
assertions: Identifies unresolved duplicate entities as the root cause
Names at least 3 of the 4 duplicate pairs (J. Okonkwo/Jane Okonkwo, ledger-api/Ledger API, Meridian Payments/MP checkout, R. Vasquez/Rosa Vasquez)
Reports that the graph splits into multiple disconnected components and states the count (4)
Prescribes an entity-resolution pass as the fix
Notes that pure string similarity is insufficient for at least one of these cases
Traces the specific failed query to the duplicates that break its path

evals.name: extraction-eval-setup
evals.prompt: i keep tweaking the prompt i use to pull entities and relationships out of documents and honestly i can't tell if it's getting better or if i'm just fooling myself. every run looks fine when i squint at it. how do i set up a way to actually measure this? my corpus is at CORPUS_PATH.
evals.expected_output: A gold-set format, an alias map for surface variants, a runnable P/R/F1 scorer, and the caveat that predicate-insensitive relation scoring is an upper bound.
assertions: Specifies a concrete gold-set file format with a worked example
Uses precision, recall, and F1 as the metrics
Includes an alias/canonicalization map so surface variants are not scored as misses
Warns that relation scoring ignoring predicate wording is an upper bound on recall
Advises hand-labeling only a small number of representative documents rather than the whole corpus
Notes run-to-run non-determinism and advises repeat runs before believing a delta
Provides a runnable scorer script
